items.title: Mozambique: 25-year Machipanda concession award suspended after SAFAGA court challenge
items.summary: The decision follows a challenge by SAFAGA, which disputes the criteria used to evaluate the bids, the reasoning behind the award, the experience and financial capacity of the winning consortium, as well as the composition of the tender evaluation committee During the evaluation process, Union Energy/Zhongmei scored 86 points, compared with 81 awarded to SAFAGA. items.title: Missiles intercepted near Riyadh after Saudi coalition hits Yemen fuel depot

items.title: Russian strikes hit key power plant in Kyiv, Zelensky says
items.summary: Firefighters work at the site of an apartment building damaged by a Russian missile strike A key energy facility supplying Kyiv with heating and electricity has been hit in a Russian ballistic missile attack, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Darnytska CHP-4, or CHPP-4, and a residential building were hit in a strike the president said came with "no early warning from our partners" Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said one person was killed and 13 injured in the missile strike on the apartment block late on Tuesday. Four people were in a serious condition, he said It comes two days after US President Donald Trump said an energy ceasefire had been agreed by Russia and Ukraine, although Kyiv reported multiple Russian strikes following the announcement "Ukraine supported an energy ceasefire.

items.title: OpenAI says employee caught planting listening device
items.summary: A Saudi national employed by the artificial intelligence lab has been arrested after a listening device was planted in a company conference room OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT , said Tuesday one of its employees was arrested after a "sophisticated recording device" was found in one of its San Francisco offices A 35-year-old Saudi national working as an engineer was arrested on Friday, a week after the device was discovered in a conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco After the device was discovered, the company reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee. A federal investigation is ongoing The suspect, who appeared in court on Tuesday, has been charged with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications The criminal complaint did not specify what the suspect might have wanted to do with the recordings.

items.title: Mozambique: IPEME and TFO Canada launch TRISEG to boost MSME growth
items.summary: Funded by the Government of Canada, the TRISEG initiative aims to strengthen micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and promote their access to international markets The event was attended by IPEME Deputy Director-General Mijóia Caetano, Canada’s Ambassador to Mozambique, Zaki Munshi, Pascale Thivierge, representing TFO Canada, and Brenda Garcia, the project manager at the same organisation The launch brought together various stakeholders to discuss the strengthening and development of MSMEs in Mozambique Running for five years (2025–2030), the TRISEG project aims to support 200 MSMEs in Mozambique, 67% of which will be owned or led by women and under-represented groups.

items.title: DR Congo: Kabila’s move towards M23 raises questions over peace
items.summary: Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political-military front that brings together the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 coalition. Analysts say it could reshape opposition to President Felix Tshisekedi Joseph Kabila's decision to lead a new political-military movement, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), puts the former president of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in more direct confrontation with President Felix Tshisekedi's government . Kabila announced the FRN on October 12 in Goma, eastern DRC, at his residence, where leaders of the AFC/M23 rebel movements joined him FRN coalition adviser, Claude Ibalanky, said the group would unite opposition forces, including figures associated with the AFC/M23 movement. The new structure succeeds the Congo River Alliance (AFC), which had been allied with the M23 rebellion. Its leadership includes former AFC leader Corneille Nangaa and M23 political leader Bertrand Bisimwa.
